title: The Cascade Tiebreak
subtitle: IDs, classes, and order of appearance.
description: Which rule wins when selectors collide?
prompt:
Given `

` and the rules `#intro { color: blue }`, `.note { color: red }`, and `p { color: green }` — plus `p.note { color: purple }` — which color applies? **A.** red — classes beat element selectors **B.** green — element selectors apply last **C.** purple — the most specific compound selector wins **D.** blue — the ID selector outranks every class-based selector regardless of order
options: purple — the most specific compound selector wins
blue — the ID selector outranks every class-based selector regardless of order
hints: Compare the three-column tuple before thinking about order.
Order matters only between selectors of EQUAL specificity.

solution.summary: The correct answer is D — blue — the ID selector outranks every class-based selector regardless of order
solution.answer: blue — the ID selector outranks every class-based selector regardless of order
reasoning: Only !important or inline styles outrank ID selectors — both are smells.
whyNot: red — classes beat element selectors — .note alone is (0,1,0) and loses to p.note, let alone #intro.
green — element selectors apply last — Element selectors are the weakest tier here.
purple — the most specific compound selector wins — p.note is (0,1,1) — strong among class rules, but zero IDs still lose to one.
